prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Phoenix after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Phoenix for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you specific firm names, but to make the list useful I need one quick piece of info: do you prefer a large, national firm with lots of resources or a smaller local/boutique firm that may give more personal attention? Also tell me your ZIP or neighborhood in Phoenix and whether your injuries are minor, moderate, or severe — that helps me tailor recommendations.

In the meantime, here’s what will help you right away and how to choose which firms to call.

Why call several firms (and how many)
- Call 3–5 firms so you can compare experience, fees, and how comfortable you feel with the attorney.
- Ask for a free initial consultation (most personal injury firms offer one) and whether they handle car-accident cases on contingency (no fee unless you recover money).

What types of firms to call and why
- Large, national or regional firms: often have more staff, immediate resources (investigators, medical experts), and experience taking big cases to trial. Good if injuries are serious or liability is contested.
- Local/boutique Phoenix firms: may provide more personalized attention, know local judges and adjusters, and be quicker to communicate. Good for straightforward cases or if you want hands-on counsel.
- Plaintiff-only personal injury firms (not defense): ensures the firm’s business model is aligned with maximizing your recovery, not minimizing it.

Essential things to ask on the call (script-ready)
- “Do you handle car-accident/personal-injury cases in Phoenix? How many in the last year?”
- “Have you handled cases like mine (describe severity and facts) — can you give an example of outcome (no guarantees)?”
- “Do you take cases on contingency? What percentage is your fee and what costs will I be responsible for if we don’t recover?”
- “Do you go to trial or do you mostly settle? What percent of your cases go to trial?”
- “Who in the firm will handle my case day to day — the attorney or a paralegal?”
- “How will you keep me updated and how quickly can I expect responses?”
- “Do you have references or client reviews I can read?”

Documents and information to have ready when you call
- Date/time/location of accident, police report number (if any)
- Photos of the scene, vehicles, injuries
- Names/contacts of witnesses
- Your insurance and other party’s insurance info
- Medical records, ER bills, treatment notes, prescriptions
- Pay stubs for lost wages, repair estimates, rental car receipts

Practical tips and red flags
- Red flags: pressure to sign immediately without explanation, vague answers about fees, no contingency option, refusal to put fee arrangement in writing.
- Good signs: clear fee agreement, written plan for investigation, trial experience, good client reviews, AV ratings or state bar disciplinary check is clean.
- Arizona statute of limitations: typically 2 years for personal injury (act promptly — there are exceptions but don’t delay).

If you want, I can now:
- Provide a short list of 4–6 specific Phoenix personal injury firms (with reasons to call each) if you tell me local vs national preference and your ZIP/neighborhood, or
- Give a sample comparison checklist you can use while you call.

Which would you prefer?
